worked_solution:
Let $u={x}^{3}+7.$ Then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3{x}^{2}\,⟹\,\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u={x}^{2}\,\text{d}x,
$$

and we can solve the resulting integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{3}+7}}\,\text{d}x & =3\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{3}+7}}\cdot {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3}{3}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\sqrt{u}+C \\  & =2\sqrt{{x}^{3}+7}+C\end{aligned}
$$
